learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand and apply eco-design concepts adapted to new situations for professional development.
Acquire environmental ethics concepts that allow an in-depth analysis of environmental issues that will affect the engineer in their professional life.
Develop strategies and procedures for solving environmental problems of products and services.
Work in a team and develop knowledge with a critical and responsible technical/cultural exchange.
Plan and manage eco-design projects according to current legislation.
Perform an ethical critique of product design.
Create industrial products and analyze their form and function from biomimetics.
Handle design software for nature-inspired shapes.
Perform a life cycle assessment on an industrial product.

syllabus_topics: Topic ETI-01: Ethical and bioethical bases of ecological ethics.
Topic ETI-02: Ethical concerns in the ecological field: sustainability and ecological justice. Ethical concerns in the technological field.
Topic ETI-03: Paradigms for addressing ecological ethics problems in engineering: anthropocentrism, biocentrism, and ecofeminism.
Topic ACV-01: Regulations. Eco-design management systems. ISO 14006.
Topic DIS-01: Business context. Motivating factors.
Topic DIS-04: Biomimetics and fractal geometry.
Topic DIS-06: Product simulation and evaluation.

assessment_methods.method: Exercises, assignments and presentations developed during the course
Active participation of the student in the development of the course

assessment_rules: Students must attend at least 80% of practical classes (classroom and laboratory) to be considered present for continuous assessment. The final grade is calculated as 0.6 * EV1 + 0.3 * EV2 + 0.1 * EV3. If minimum attendance is not met, or if the calculated grade is less than 4.0, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. For extraordinary evaluation, students must take a written test and submit an individual assignment, each weighted at 50%.
